newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada's Chretien trails local separatist-poll.
newsitem.headline: Canada's Chretien trails local separatist-poll.

text.p: Canadian Prime Minister Jean Chretien is less popular than a Quebec separatist candidate in his home electoral district, said a survey prepared for the opposition candidate, a newspaper reported on Friday.

Montreal French-language newspaper Le Devoir said the poll of 663 voters in Chretien's riding of Saint-Maurice, Quebec showed separatist Bloc Quebecois candidate Yves Duhaime leading Chretien by 49.6 percent to 39.6 percent, with the Conservative candidate at 6.3 percent. The poll was taken on January 31 and February 1. The margin of error was not given.
A Canadian election could be called as early as June.

Duhaime, a former Quebec government cabinet minister, is one of six Bloc Quebecois candidates seeking the leadership of the separatist party, which is the official opposition in Canada's House of Commons.
Duhaime has not been officially nominated as the Bloc Quebecois candidate in Chretien's district.
In the 1993 federal election, Chretien won 54.1 percent of the vote in his riding, followed by a different Bloc Quebecois candidate with 40.5 percent.
